A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same tournament-based LLM evaluation work, renamed from VARCO Arena to Arena-Lite. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation and LLM-judge experiments, including ranking correlations, model-insertion results, and confidence-interval separability analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds extended judge-by-prompt-count results in Appendix A.2 and evaluation examples in the web-demo screenshots.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds power-of-two bracket padding, explicit bye handling, and winner–loser result recording, refining the existing randomized tournament procedure. The Elo-to-Bradley–Terry terminology change alone does not establish a different estimator: v2 already describes logistic fitting with the same win-probability formula.

E1.justification: The main simulation and Arena-Hard-Auto coverage remain. New Appendix A.1 screenshots show a six-row evaluation involving Korean rewriting and four model variants, adding a small language/task example. The starter-prompt catalog does not establish additional systematic benchmark evaluations.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison remains tournament ranking versus baseline-output win rates. New-model insertion still compares binary search with top-model anchoring. Newly discussed methods such as UniCBE and JuStRank are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported candidate count from 20 to 19 and available outputs from 21 to 20 including the baseline, aligning the text with Figure 3's existing 19-model label. This does not establish a rerun. Table 4 newly reports smaller-prompt settings for the existing non-GPT judges; Appendix A.1 also documents a separate six-row, four-model demo.

E4.justification: New Table 4 extends prompt-count sensitivity analysis to Claude, Llama, Qwen, and Gemma judges, previously tabulated only at 500 prompts. Demo screenshots additionally illustrate match statistics and position/length-bias diagnostics. The earlier insertion and confidence-interval separability analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 50 simulation trials, 500 empirical trials, and bootstrap-based 95% confidence intervals. However, v4 newly describes Figure 3 as summarizing 50 runs, contradicting its retained 500-trial empirical descriptions. This changes run-count reporting without establishing that the number of runs actually changed.

E6.justification: Main Tables 2–3 and the relocated insertion tables retain their values. New Table 4 adds results such as Qwen2.5-7B correlations of 0.492 for the baseline and 0.544 for Arena-Lite at 50 prompts; v2 tabulated that judge only at 500 prompts. Demo outcomes are also added. Table 4 reports Gemma2-2B at 500 prompts as 0.551, conflicting with 0.552 retained in Table 3.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces v2's claimed per-pair lower bound of |X|/[2(nmodel−1)] with an average range from |X|/(nmodel−1) to |X|log2(nmodel)/(nmodel−1), revising the mathematical sampling argument. It also clarifies per-model comparison bounds. The probability equations and prompt-independence assumption remain; no rigorous new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that randomized single-elimination comparisons avoid fixed reference outputs and produce reliable human-aligned rankings with fewer comparisons. Small-dataset and weak-judge robustness receive greater prominence in v4, but these claims and the demo/code contribution were already present in v2.

C2.justification: The introduction adds weak transitivity of preferences as an explanation for noise in baseline-mediated comparisons. Existing interpretations concerning weak judges and bracket randomness remain. Appendix A.6.1 retains the recommendation for anchored insertion but removes v2 A.4.1's budget-based explanation of binary search's shortcomings.

D1.justification: v2's demo/code URL placeholders are replaced by a concrete access location and a substantial new appendix describing the hostable web demo, result inspection, bias diagnostics, and configurable starter prompts with documentation/YAML links. Existing hardware, cached-judgment procedures, evaluation prompt, and decoding disclosures remain. External resource availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially repositions the work: discussion of Elo benchmarking and reference-free metrics such as RAGElo and XCOMET is replaced by system-ranking research and efficient evaluation, including JuStRank, DIoR, UniCBE, BenchBench, and tinyBenchmarks. Bradley–Terry and non-transitivity references also support the revised framing.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the method, v4 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, preliminaries, experimental exposition, related work, and conclusion. Section 3.3 becomes a structured four-part argument, terminology shifts toward baseline-mediated comparisons and BT ratings, and the appendix is reorganized around new demo and extended-results sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Table 1 receives different comparison columns and moves to the introduction, and four web-demo screenshots plus a full-page extended-results table are added. Existing plots receive revised legends, labels, captions, and separability annotations. The insertion summary moves into the appendix, whose displays are substantially rearranged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves usability and contextual clarity through concrete demo/code access information, clearer rating terminology, more relevant related work, and extended judge-sensitivity results. These are useful gains while the central experimental evidence remains largely unchanged. New inconsistencies between Figure 3's 50 runs and the stated 500 trials, and between Gemma scores in Tables 3–4, limit the improvement.
